questions.prompt: Trace a single paragraph edit from keystroke to SQLite, including what happens when the save request fails.

keyPoints.text: Typing calls the store's updateBlock action.
keyPoints.quote: `onChange` calls `store.updateBlock(...)` in `workspaceStore`.

keyPoints.text: The UI re-renders immediately from local Zustand state.
keyPoints.quote: UI updates immediately from local Zustand state (fast perceived response).

keyPoints.text: A debounced autosave PUTs the serialized workspace.
keyPoints.quote: Debounced autosave effect in `WorkspaceApp` builds `payload` and `PUT`s `/api/workspace`.

keyPoints.text: The route only checks a minimal shape: a pages array and a blocksByPage object.
keyPoints.quote: API route validates minimal shape

keyPoints.text: sqlite.js writes the full JSON state, not a diff.
keyPoints.quote: writes full JSON state into `workspace_state` table

keyPoints.text: A failed save is queued in IndexedDB and replayed when back online or on next load.
keyPoints.quote: payload is queued in IndexedDB (`queueSync`) and replayed on `online` and on the next load

keyPoints.text: Even a queued save shows 'Saved' because the finally block updates lastSavedAt.
keyPoints.quote: The `finally` block still updates `lastSavedAt`

questions.prompt: Why do two tabs opened on the same saved workspace ignore each other's live edits, and why does the server copy usually win at startup?

keyPoints.text: State is broadcast to other tabs 500 ms after a change.
keyPoints.quote: The state is also posted on `BroadcastChannel` 500 ms after the change.

keyPoints.text: A receiving tab applies it only when the sender's meta.updatedAt is newer.
keyPoints.quote: The receiving tab applies it only if the sender's `meta.updatedAt` is newer

keyPoints.text: Client edits never move meta.updatedAt, so same-origin tabs never look newer to each other.
keyPoints.quote: Because client edits never change `meta.updatedAt`

keyPoints.text: Bootstrap picks between server state and the IndexedDB draft by meta.updatedAt.
keyPoints.quote: chooses newest by `meta.updatedAt`

keyPoints.text: Only the server stamps the timestamp, so a draft can tie but never beat the server copy.
keyPoints.quote: a draft's timestamp can equal the server's but not exceed it

keyPoints.text: If the server request fails, bootstrap fails instead of falling back to the draft.
keyPoints.quote: the whole bootstrap fails and the app shows an error rather than the draft

keyPoints.text: The client never reads the server's new timestamp back after saving.
keyPoints.quote: it does not read the server's new `meta.updatedAt` back into the store

questions.prompt: How is responsibility split across the app's modules, and which deliberate shortcuts keep it an MVP rather than a production system?

keyPoints.text: WorkspaceApp is the main UI shell and orchestrates behavior.
keyPoints.quote: main UI shell and behavior orchestration

keyPoints.text: The Zustand store owns client state and the mutation actions.
keyPoints.quote: client-side app state and state mutation actions

keyPoints.text: sqlite.js handles bootstrap, schema creation and read/write helpers.
keyPoints.quote: SQLite bootstrap, schema creation, data read/write helpers

keyPoints.text: offlineStore keeps an IndexedDB queue and drafts for offline mode.
keyPoints.quote: IndexedDB queue + draft storage for offline mode

keyPoints.text: The intentional shortcuts are a single seeded workspace, no auth and full-state saves.
keyPoints.quote: single workspace seed, no auth, full-state saves

keyPoints.text: A GET can write: a missing workspace is seeded on read.
keyPoints.quote: so this "read" can write
